Java is a high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language that was originally developed by Sun Microsystems and released in 1995. 
 It is currently owned by Oracle Corporation. 
 Java was designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. 
Its core principle is WORA: 
 Write Once, Run Anywhere. 
 This is possible thanks to the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which allows compiled Java code to run on any platform that supports Java without the need for recompilation. 
 Key Features of Java:
 1. Object-Oriented: Everything in Java is an object, which makes the code structured and reusable. 
 2. Platform Independent: Java bytecode can run on any operating system. 
 3. Robust and Secure: Java has strong memory management and built-in security features. 
 Use of Java in Android: Java was the official language for Android app development. 
 Understanding Java is essential for any computer science student to build native Android applications. 
 This app demonstrates a basic Android UI using Java
